# json-notes

> A free, open-source, browser-only tool for documenting an undocumented JSON API. You
> drop in a sample response and write down what each field means, key by key. It is not a
> JSON viewer or a schema generator — the point is the notes you author and keep.

Use it when a third party ships an API whose documentation does not match the payload,
and you have to work out the meaning of several hundred fields by reading a sample.

## What it does

- Renders a payload as a tree and lets you write a note against **any** key, including
  container keys, so a whole section can be described at its root.
- Three marks per key: `*` interesting, `?` open question, `–` ignore. Marking a
  container `–` settles everything beneath it, so a block of 50 unused fields is
  dismissed in one click.
- Tracks progress as `N keys · N marked · N untriaged` over unique paths, so you can tell
  how much of a payload you have actually read.
- Filtering to `?` gives you the list of questions to send back to the vendor — for an
  undocumented API, that list is half the output.
- Annotating a key also settles the containers above it, all the way up — having written
  something inside a section, you have plainly been in it, so it stops counting as
  untriaged. Derived, never stored.
- Several keys can be selected with `space` or shift-click and annotated together: one
  mark, or **one note written to every one of them**.
- Writing `@some-feature` in a note links that key to something you need to build.
  Features can be grouped into named sets, and each payload is told which features and
  sets apply to it. Status is then answered **per payload** — **missing** (applicable
  here, nothing here links it), **unresolved** (a linked key here is still a question),
  or **covered** — and shown as a strip of chips on that payload's tab, gaps first.
- Annotations are keyed by a normalized path with array indices collapsed
  (`authorships[].institutions[].ror`), so a repeated record is documented once rather
  than per item — and notes reattach when you load a newer sample of the same endpoint.
- Full keyboard control; search matches keys, paths and values and jumps to a match in
  its surrounding context.

## Privacy

Runs entirely in the browser. Payloads and notes live in IndexedDB and are never
transmitted; the app ships a `connect-src 'none'` Content-Security-Policy, so network
requests are blocked by the browser rather than merely avoided by convention. Relevant
for payloads containing personal data.

## Getting the notes out

Browser storage does not mean the notes are stuck in one profile. The `↓ export` button
in the toolbar writes a single JSON bundle holding every payload alongside all marks,
notes and features — one file, so treat it as carrying whatever customer data the samples
do. Dropping a bundle back on the window restores it, on any browser or machine, which is
also how the field docs reach a teammate. Imports merge and existing annotations win, so
restoring an older backup cannot clobber newer work; bundles carrying no payloads still
import. Exports matter because browsers can evict site data under pressure — the reason
the button is in the toolbar rather than in a menu.

Persistent storage is the only permission requested, and it is asked once, after a
payload of your own is open, with the reason attached — never on load. Refusing is
supported: nothing stops working, the app distinguishes a refusal from the browser
quietly declining (the permission state is read separately, since `persist()` returns
only a boolean), and it does not ask again. The `⋯` menu reports storage usage, the
current state, and keeps the explanation reachable.

The bundle is JSON. There is no markdown, JSONC or spreadsheet export.

## Links

- [App](https://christinitty-ditto.github.io/json-notes/app/): the tool itself
- [Sample payload](https://christinitty-ditto.github.io/json-notes/app/?demo): opens with a real OpenAlex API response (559 unique paths)
- [Source](https://github.com/christinitty-ditto/json-notes): MIT licensed
- [Scope](https://github.com/christinitty-ditto/json-notes/blob/main/SCOPE.md): the design, and what is deliberately left out

## Not

Not a JSON viewer, formatter, graph visualiser, schema generator, or OpenAPI converter.
Those tell you a payload's structure. This is for recording its meaning, which no tool
can infer for you.
